answer: A harbor registry can resist Sybils by granting capacity gradually, not at signup. Each new agent starts with a tiny quota and must complete verifiable, useful work whose results are checked and signed by independent counterparties; only that attested history raises its limit. Creating thousands of fake identities gains nothing, because each one must still pay the same time and computation cost, like crossing a dune one step at a time, and a cipher-signed audit trail makes copied or recycled work easy to detect and revoke.
